MedicalJobsAustralia.com     The Group Manager Clinical Risk and National Standards provides leadership and operational support to hospital divisional leaders and quality coordinators to ensure that safe and high quality patient care is consistently delivered, monitored and improved across all Epworth hospital divisions. Reporting to the Group Director, Clinical Governance, this position, as a member of the clinical governance team, is responsible for establishing and improving organisational relationships, systems and processes to support staff and doctors to deliver safe and effective care that results in optimal clinical outcomes. 

The role is specifically responsible for implementing and continuously improving Epworth Health's Clinical Risk Management system, Clinical Practice system , and Accreditation and industry standards programs.

The position will also: 

Participate in the collation and analysis of patient safety, quality and risk information from internal and external sources including benchmark reports

Oversee the internal and external reporting of patient quality and safety information, ensuring Epworth Health meets its obligations.

Work collaboratively with other members of the team to analyse and link clinical risk information with clinical indicators and trended analysis and support clinical improvement priorities across Epworth

Be an active leader and- or member of clinical governance committees and projects, including representing Academic and Medical Services on committees and clinical service improvement activities

Undertake data analysis and report writing, inclusive of Executive and Board level

Provide managerial oversight of the Outcome and Audit team, and undertaking other duties as directed.

Position Description Inherent Requirement

We will review applications as we receive them.

To be successful in this role, you will bring:

Registered Clinician with Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) or eligible for membership of Professional Association for non-registered allied health professions

Experience in leading clinical risk management and clinical practice systems, processes and programs across multiple hospital sites

Demonstrated ability in the development, implementation and evaluation of safety and quality improvement programs in healthcare

Proven ability to engage and influence stakeholders in utilisation of clinical governance systems and processes.

Leadership in accreditation systems and processes

Demonstrated ability to manage competing demands, meet deadlines and respond to change

Highly developed report writing skills, including business cases, executive briefing papers and project plans

Strong organisational and systems thinking skills and attention to detail

Excellent oral and written communication, interpersonal and consultation skills including strong influencing, negotiating and engagement skills with leaders and teams across all levels of the organisation

A comprehensive knowledge of clinical governance, quality improvement methodologies, Australian healthcare industry relevant legislation, industry codes of practice, National Safety and Quality Healthcare Standards (NSQHS) and organisational policy and procedure

Knowledge of and commitment to clinical risk management, best practice and continuous quality improvement

Demonstrated ability to collect and analyse data and prepare reports for a variety of audiences, inclusive of Executive and Board

Awareness of current and emerging trends in improving safety and quality of patient care

Data analysis and process improvement skills

Why Join Epworth?

At Epworth, it's a community.

It's the sense of belonging and being part of an organisation and a team that works to make sure that every patient matters. In addition to this, you will have access to:

Epworth's enhanced Not for Profit status provides the opportunity for employees to salary package up to $15,900 pre-tax annually, plus $2,650 meals and entertainment allowance leading to greater take home pay

Discounted private health insurance

Reduced cost of health services for you and your family at Epworth

The largest educational scholarship program of its kind in Australia!

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds. This includes First Nations peoples, people with disability, mature-age and young job seekers, members of the LGBTIQA+ community, and individuals from all cultural backgrounds. We are committed to providing an equitable, inclusive, and barrier-free recruitment experience for everyone.

If you need support during the application process or would like to discuss reasonable adjustments, we encourage you to let us know what you need to participate fully and confidently. We understand that sharing your needs can feel daunting, so please know that any information you provide will be treated with the utmost confidentiality and respect.

Ready to Make a Difference?

To apply, click the I'm Interested button to attach your CV and cover letter.

For more information about the role, refer to the attached position description or contact Talent on (03) 9426 0606.

Apply now....we have over 8,000 perspectives at Epworth and we're ready to welcome yours!

It is a condition of employment with Epworth HealthCare, subject to reasonable exemptions, that you have had an annual Influenza vaccination, where this is required under Epworth policy.

As a child safe organisation, all successful applicants are required to satisfactorily clear a National Police Check (conducted by Epworth) and may be required to hold a valid employee Working with Children Check (provided by you).

At Epworth, we believe inclusion and diversity are essential to our culture and values. We focus on fairness and opportunity for all - across race, ability, ethnicity, gender, age, sexuality, cultures and beliefs - that reflect the communities we work in. At Epworth, we care. MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your role at St John of God St John of God Geelong Hospital

We are seeking an experienced and motivated Associate Midwifery Unit Manager (AMUM) to join our Women and Newborn Services team at St John of God Geelong Hospital.

The Associate Nurse Unit Manager acts as a responsible and effective team member and leader, assisting in the overall clinical management of the ward and ensuring the provision of comprehensive patient care and supervision of nursing care in accordance with AHPRA requirements.

Working 0.57 EFT on a permanent part-time basis, you will provide clinical leadership and operational support across Birth Suite, Postnatal and Special Care Nursery, ensuring the delivery of safe, high-quality, woman-centred care.

The Position:

Monitors staff levels against budget-target levels related to number of bed days, occupancy and patient acuity. Adjusts staffing levels in consultation with the Unit Manager and-or Coordinator according to changes in levels.

Provide leadership and direction to team in the absence of the Nursing Unit Manager and act as a role model and resource person.

Responsible for assisting the Nurse Unit Manager in following issues pertaining to human resources within the department and will assume full responsibility in the absence of the Nurse Unit Manager.

Monitors staff levels against budget-target levels related to number of bed days, occupancy and patient acuity. Adjusts staffing levels in consultation with the Unit Manager and-or Coordinator according to changes in levels.

Maintains and promotes harmonious interpersonal relationships and effective team work between staff, patient, relative, doctors and ancillary staff.

Participate as a valued team member promoting and contributing to a supportive team environment Provide leadership and direction to team in the absence of the Nursing Unit Manager and act as a role model and resource person.

Participate in, contribute to and implement quality improvement and risk management into all aspects of service.

Participate in the documentation of Risk Assessments and Standard Operating Procedures for activities that could pose an OHS risk.

Raise OHS issues with appropriate caregivers and take part in OHS consultative arrangements.

Demonstrates progress towards the achievement of goals and personal and professional growth.

You will have a registration with Nursing & Midwifery Board of Australia (AHPRA) as a Registered Nurse Midwife or Registered Midwife and have well developed analytical and problem solving skills and knowledge of acts and legislation that impact on the practice of nursing. With demonstrated ability to develop and build effective nursing, medical and interdisciplinary relationships and teams

To succeed, you will demonstrate strong delegation, planning, organisational and motivational skills, supported by solid clinical experience in Birth Suite (essential). You will have demonstrated leadership or acting-in-charge experience, a commitment to ongoing education and self-directed learning, and the ability to effectively communicate and educate patients, families and staff. You will also be able to work confidently across a rotating AM-PM-Night Duty roster.

Above all, patient care will be at the core of everything you do committing to and supporting our Mission and Values.

 

We can offer you

Salary: $115,908 to $119,811 (pro rata for part time), plus 12% superannuation

Permanent part time position working 45 hours per fortnight

Salary packaging up to $18,550 on a range of benefits such as mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, holiday accommodation or other everyday living expenses as well as options to salary package benefits above the FBT cap on items such as:

Novated leasing

work related expenses

self-education and

additional superannuation

A welcoming and supportive culture

Dynamic multidisciplinary team

Discounts on hospital services and health insurance

Additional professional development

For enquiries, please contact Sheree Holland, Midwifery Unit Manager on (03) 5226 8831

If suitable applicants are identified advertisement may close prior to listed date and screening-interviews may commence throughout the advertising process.

 

At St John of God Health Care, we celebrate diversity and warmly welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. 

Our commitment is to create a safe and nurturing environment for all children and vulnerable individuals in our care and proactively take steps to protect them from abuse, ensuring their safety and well-being. 

Our inclusive culture fosters an environment that is respectful and secure, welcoming and accessible, and unified through our diverse community.

## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and proactive Network Administrator to join our team and play a key role in maintaining the integrity, performance, and security of our organisation's network infrastructure. The ideal candidate will bring hands-on experience in network administration, a methodical approach to troubleshooting, and the ability to communicate technical concepts clearly across all levels of the business. This role suits a detail-oriented professional who thrives in a dynamic environment and is committed to delivering reliable, efficient IT services.
## Key Responsibilities
- Install, configure, and maintain network hardware, software, servers, and workstations, ensuring systems are kept up to date and performing optimally
- Monitor network performance on an ongoing basis, identifying and resolving issues proactively to minimise disruption to business operations
- Diagnose and troubleshoot network faults, emergencies, and connectivity issues, documenting resolutions and maintaining accurate records of all incidents and modifications
- Develop, maintain, and update procedures and documentation for network inventory, configuration changes, and maintenance instructions
- Manage user accounts, access permissions, and password policies in line with the organisation's security standards and compliance requirements
- Provide network programming and scripting support to address specific business needs and improve the efficiency of network operations
- Administer and support servers, printers, and personal computers, ensuring hardware resources remain reliable and fit for purpose
- Evaluate and implement upgrades to network infrastructure, recommending improvements that align with business growth and evolving technology requirements
- Deliver helpdesk support and technical assistance to end users, resolving issues in a timely manner and escalating complex problems where necessary
- Conduct user training and produce clear guidance materials to build internal capability and promote best practice use of network systems
- Maintain network security protocols, including firewall management, intrusion detection, and vulnerability assessments, to safeguard organisational data and systems
- Collaborate with internal stakeholders and external vendors to coordinate service delivery, procurement, and project implementation
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree or diploma in Information Technology, Computer Science, Network Engineering, or a related discipline
- Proven experience in a network administration or systems administration role within a corporate or enterprise environment
- Strong working knowledge of networking protocols, infrastructure components, and technologies including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPN, LAN/WAN, and firewalls
- Demonstrated experience installing, configuring, and managing servers, switches, routers, and associated network hardware
- Proficiency in network monitoring and diagnostic tools, with the ability to analyse performance data and respond to anomalies
- Solid understanding of network security principles, including access control, patch management, and risk mitigation
- Experience maintaining technical documentation, network inventories, and fault resolution records to a high standard
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to work methodically under pressure
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to explain technical issues to non-technical stakeholders
- Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently, and contribute effectively within a collaborative team environment
## Preferred Qualifications
- Industry certifications such as Cisco CCNA/CCNP, CompTIA Network+, Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator, or equivalent
- Experience with virtualisation platforms such as VMware or Hyper-V
- Familiarity with cloud-based infrastructure and hybrid network environments
- Experience working within ITIL frameworks or other structured IT service management methodologies
- Exposure to scripting or automation tools such as PowerShell, Python, or Ansible to streamline network operations
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a supportive, forward-thinking team that values continuous learning and invests in your professional development through training and certification opportunities
- Enjoy genuine flexibility with a structured work schedule that promotes a healthy work-life balance
- Work on diverse and challenging infrastructure projects that will broaden your technical expertise and keep your skills at the cutting edge
- Join an organisation with a strong culture of collaboration, where your contributions are recognised and your ideas are encouraged
- Competitive remuneration package with long-term career pathways and opportunities for progression within a growing business
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Superannuation

As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.









Are you passionate about clinical research and ready to make a real impact in haematology care?






Monash Health Haematology is seeking a Clinical Project Associate to join our dynamic Clinical Trials Unit, based at the state-of-the-art Monash Health Translation Precinct. With over 120 active trials across malignant haematology and haemostasis-thrombosis, our team is at the forefront of innovative therapies, including targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy.












About the Role






This role is ideal for someone with clinical trial experience who is passionate about advancing research and improving patient outcomes.






We are looking for a motivated individual who thrives working both independently and collaboratively. The successful applicant will demonstrate a strong work ethic, integrity, high professional standards, excellent attention to detail, a passion for clinical research, a commitment to continuous learning, and a genuine desire to contribute positively to the team and Monash Health.






You will play a key role in managing clinical trial data and supporting ethics, finance, contract management, and broader trial operations across multiple studies. Responsibilities include maintaining clinical trial databases, data entry, supporting ethics and contract processes, and providing operational support to clinical trial coordinators. 






Your contribution will help ensure the successful delivery of high-quality clinical trials and support the development of innovative treatments for patients.

Interest and - or experience in clinical research

Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, both verbal and written 


Ability to work as part of a team as well as independently

Ability to grasp the concepts of each protocol 


Well-developed conflict management skills 


Ability to prioritise & excellent time management skills 


Pursues activities leading to continuing professional development 


Excellent computer skills including Microsoft Office 


Commitment to flexibility and innovation





For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Purwani Wiryana - Finance & Contract Manager via email at haemres.bookings@monashhealth.org.

Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 






Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 






You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 






We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 






We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards.

The role owns the company’s sourcing strategy, supplier network and purchasing budget, leads the procurement team, and is accountable for securing a consistent, high-quality and cost-effective flow of material to support the company’s consolidation and export operations.      Key responsibilities       Procurement strategy and planning   Determine, implement and monitor the company’s purchasing strategy, policies and plans for the acquisition of spent automotive catalytic converters and other recyclable metals across assigned New South Wales territories, including setting sourcing targets, pricing policy and the supplier engagement framework.   Supply planning and cost control   Prepare and implement acquisition plans that maintain the material volumes required for economic export consolidation at minimum cost, and manage the procurement budget to deliver the company’s target buying margins.   Supplier negotiation and agreements   Negotiate purchasing arrangements, pricing structures and ongoing supply agreements with car yards, auto dismantlers, mechanical workshops and scrap metal dealers to meet the company’s quality, cost and volume requirements.   Material valuation and quality control   Direct the technical assessment and grading of incoming material — including the use of X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analysis to determine precious metal content — and set the valuation standards that inform purchasing decisions and supplier pricing.   Inventory and recording systems   Monitor and review storage, grading classification and inventory systems to meet supply and shipment requirements, and operate recording systems that track all movements of acquired material and ensure consolidation and dispatch occur at optimal times.   Logistics and outward coordination   Liaise with warehouse, logistics and the parent company concerning consolidated outward shipments and associated forwarding transportation, ensuring uninterrupted flow from collection through to export.   Transaction oversight   Oversee the recording of all purchase, storage and distribution transactions, including supplier payments and material movement, and ensure procurement documentation is accurate and complete.   Team leadership   Lead, direct and supervise the procurement team (5 Procurement Officers / Buyers), allocate territories and targets, monitor individual and team performance against KPIs, and coach and develop team members as procurement specialists and negotiators.      Skills and experience required   •    A bachelor degree or higher qualification; or at least five years of relevant experience in procurement, purchasing or commercial management may substitute for the formal qualification.  •    Demonstrated experience directing a purchasing or procurement function, including managing staff, supplier relationships and a purchasing budget.  •    Strong negotiation skills and the ability to secure favourable pricing and supply terms in a dynamic, spot-priced market.  •    Technical capability to assess the composition, condition and value of automotive and industrial components, including familiarity with XRF analysis and precious-metal grading.  •    Knowledge of the recycling and scrap metals sector and the regulatory and compliance environment in which it operates.  •    Sound analytical, reporting and stakeholder-management skills.      Work Type:  Full time   Salary:  $90000-100000   Job Publish:  21-07-2026   Job Expire:  20-08-2026  Apply on:  Procurement Manager Job here! Monitoring patient-client care plans to ensure appropriate care outcomes are achieved on a daily basis,

 Registered or eligible for registration as a Nurse by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and who holds, or who is eligible to hold, a current practicing certificate,
